content: A blackhead, medically referred to as an open comedo (plural: comedones), is a small bump or plug on the skin that appears yellowish or blackish in color. It is a specific type of acne vulgaris. Blackheads form due to the accumulation of excess oils within the duct of the sebaceous gland. The primary causes of blackheads include an overproduction of oil and the use of makeup, both of which can create an environment conducive to the proliferation of Cutibacterium acnes (formerly known as Propionibacterium acnes), a predominant anaerobic bacterium that is part of the normal skin flora. The material found within blackheads is primarily composed of keratin and modified sebum, which is an oily secretion produced by the sebaceous glands. This material darkens in appearance due to oxidation, giving it a dirt-like appearance. Blackheads can be professionally extracted by a trained medical professional, such as a dermatologist, using sterilized instruments specifically designed for blackhead removal. It is strongly advised not to pick at or remove blackheads without proper sterilized tools, as this can lead to skin damage or infection. For further details on the causes and treatment of blackheads, refer to comprehensive information on acne vulgaris.
